title: The Man Who Flew Ten Thousand Times On One Ticket
sources: Los Angeles Times / The Guardian / Wikipedia — American Airlines sold unlimited lifetime first-class AAirpasses for $250,000 in the 1980s (plus $150,000 companion option).

Forbes / Business Insider — Steve Rothstein bought an AAirpass in 1987, took over 10,000 flights (30+ million miles) including trips to other cities just for lunch, costing the airline an estimated $21 million before revocation in 2008.

lines.text: In 1987, one man bought an unlimited lifetime plane ticket —
lines.caps: In 1987, | one man | bought an | unlimited | lifetime | plane ticket —

lines.text: and flew ten thousand times on the airline's dime.
See, American Airlines badly needed cash in the eighties,
so they offered a wild golden pass for two hundred fifty thousand dollars.
Unlimited first class, anywhere on Earth, forever.
Investor Steve Rothstein happily paid up,
lines.caps: Investor | Steve Rothstein | happily | paid up,

lines.text: then turned airports into his personal subway.
He flew to London just for lunch,
and even booked an empty companion seat under the name Bag Rothstein.
Over twenty years he racked up thirty million miles,
costing the airline twenty-one million dollars in free seats.
Eventually an airport agent walked up, confiscated his golden card,
lines.caps: Eventually | an airport agent | walked up, | confiscated | his golden card,

lines.text: and banned him for exploiting their own promise.
Only sixty-six people bought the pass — and Steve won the record.
